title: Take the answer only if it suits you.
subtitle: Shopping for a ruling, and words without hearts
then: The Prophet ﷺ is comforted: {idea}do not let them grieve you.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says some said we believe with their mouths while their hearts had no faith. Others came for a ruling and agreed among themselves: {trap}if he gives the easy answer, take it, and if not, refuse it.{/trap}
now: You ask three friends until one says what you wanted to hear. You search online until one video agrees with you. {trap}The answer was chosen before the question.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks if you are seeking truth or permission.{/idea}
old: I just want to hear one opinion that says I am fine.
new: Asking only to hear what suits me is not seeking guidance at all.
try: Think of one question you keep asking until you get the answer you like. Ask Allah for the truth instead.

title: If you judge, judge with justice. Allah loves the just.
subtitle: What you listen to and what you consume
then: The verse describes people who were {trap}eager listeners to falsehood and eager consumers of what is unlawful.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ was told he could judge between them or turn away, and that if he judged, {idea}judge with justice, for Allah loves the just.{/idea}
now: The podcast full of rumors you keep playing. The side income you know is not clean. {trap}What you feed your ears and your stomach shapes you.{/trap} And when two friends ask you to settle a fight, {idea}be fair, even to the one you like less.{/idea}
old: What I listen to and where my money comes from is my own business.
new: What I take in shapes my heart, and fairness is owed even when I am the judge.
try: Unfollow or mute one source that mostly feeds you gossip or lies today.

title: Why ask, when you already hold the answer?
subtitle: Seeking judgment while turning from guidance you have
then: Ibn Kathir explains that these people came to the Prophet ﷺ for a ruling, though {idea}they had Allah's judgment in their own scripture.{/idea} The question in the verse is gentle and sharp: how? And then {trap}they turned away even after that.{/trap}
now: You ask your friend whether you should apologize to your mother. You already know. You ask the imam about that deal at work. {trap}You already know.{/trap} {idea}Often the problem is not knowledge but willingness.{/idea}
old: I am not sure what is right. I need more opinions.
new: Most of the time I already know what is right. The step is following it.
try: Pick one thing you already know you should do and have been asking about. Do it instead of asking.

title: Fear Me, not people, and do not sell My verses cheaply.
subtitle: Guarding revelation when it costs you
then: The verse honors the Torah: {reward}guidance and light{/reward}, by which prophets and scholars judged, because {idea}they were entrusted with Allah's Book.{/idea} The warning to everyone who carries a scripture: {trap}do not fear people, and do not exchange My verses for a small price.{/trap}
now: Your manager wants you to sign off on something dishonest. Your friends laugh at something you know is wrong. {trap}Staying quiet keeps the job and the friends.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks whose reaction you fear more.{/idea}
old: A little silence about the truth is the price of getting along.
new: Trading what Allah said for people's approval is a very cheap sale.
try: In one small moment today, say the honest thing gently, even if it costs you a little approval.

title: Justice is equal. Forgiving it is charity.
subtitle: A right given, and the reward of letting it go

row.title: equal justice
sub: harm for harm, same for all

key.label: What you can do with a right

then: Ibn Kathir says the law was meant to {idea}treat everyone equally and fairly.{/idea} Then the verse opens a door: whoever gives up the right as charity, it is expiation. The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever forgives a wound done to him, {reward}Allah will pardon him something similar.{/reward}
now: Your cousin damaged your car and never paid. Your coworker embarrassed you in front of everyone. {idea}You have every right to demand it back.{/idea} The verse does not cancel your right. It shows you {reward}a better use for it.{/reward}
old: If I let it go, I am letting them win.
new: My right is real, and giving it up for Allah becomes charity that covers my own faults.
try: Forgive one small debt or wrong someone owes you today, and tell Allah you did it for Him.

title: Isa came confirming what came before him.
subtitle: One chain of guidance and light
then: Ibn Kathir says Isa {idea}believed in the Torah and ruled by it.{/idea} The Gospel he received was {reward}a guidance that directs to the truth and a light that removes doubts{/reward}, and an admonition for those mindful of Allah.
now: You may think of faith as something that started with you or your family. {idea}It is part of a long chain of messengers{/idea}, each confirming the last. Every time you pray, you join a line much older than you.
old: Each messenger came with a completely separate message.
new: The messengers came in one line, confirming each other, all pointing to the same Lord.
try: Read about one earlier prophet today and notice what his message shares with the Quran.

title: Live by what you say you believe.
subtitle: Holding a book is not the same as following it
then: Ibn Kathir explains that this means {idea}to believe in all that is in it and follow all its commands{/idea}, including its good news of a coming messenger. Those who did not were called {trap}rebellious, preferring falsehood and abandoning truth.{/trap}
now: The Quran sits on your shelf in a nice cover. You know its words are true. {trap}But how much of your week is shaped by it?{/trap} The verse addresses one people, but {idea}the question fits every person who holds a book from Allah.{/idea}
old: Having the Quran at home and believing in it is enough.
new: A book from Allah is meant to shape my decisions, not just sit on my shelf.
try: Choose one verse you know well and let it guide one decision you make today.

title: He could have made you one. Instead: race to do good.
subtitle: The Quran as guardian, and differences as a test
then: Ibn Abbas said muhaymin means {idea}trustworthy, a witness, and guardian{/idea} over the earlier books. The verse says Allah could have made everyone one community, but chose {trap}to test you with what He gave you.{/trap} So {reward}race to good.{/reward} He will explain the differences on return.
now: The comment section where everyone argues about religion. The family dinner that turns into a debate. {trap}Hours spent proving you are right.{/trap} {idea}The verse says: spend that energy racing to do good, and leave the final word to Allah.{/idea}
old: Winning the argument is the most important thing.
new: Differences are a test, and my answer is to race in good deeds while Allah settles the rest.
try: Skip one argument today, online or at home, and spend that time doing a good deed instead.

title: Beware of being pulled away from part of the guidance.
subtitle: Pressure to drop some of what Allah revealed
then: Even the Prophet ﷺ is told: {trap}beware lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah revealed.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says this means not following {idea}the ideas people promote{/idea} that turn them from revelation. The danger is not all at once, but {trap}some of it.{/trap}
now: Friends at work say: just skip the prayer for this meeting. Others say: everyone bends the truth a little on these forms. {trap}Each time it is only a small part.{/trap} {idea}Notice how much gets dropped one small part at a time.{/idea}
old: Giving up one small part to fit in does not really change anything.
new: Guidance is lost a piece at a time, so I hold on to each piece.
try: Pick one practice you have quietly dropped to fit in. Bring it back today, calmly.

title: Who judges better than Allah, for those who are certain?
subtitle: Old customs versus guidance
then: This verse closes the passage on judging by revelation. The question points back to {trap}the judgment of the time of ignorance{/trap}, the customs before guidance came. Then: {idea}who is better than Allah in judgment, for a people who are certain?{/idea}
now: The family feud nobody remembers the reason for, kept alive for years. The tradition of a wedding that leaves a young couple in debt. {trap}Because that is how we have always done it.{/trap} {idea}Certainty in Allah lets you question the custom.{/idea}
old: Our customs are part of who we are, so they must be right.
new: When a custom and Allah's guidance differ, His judgment is the better one.
try: Name one custom in your family or culture that you have never checked against the Quran. Look into it.
